summary: Sanpakoi Kanomjeen is a casual, cash-only stall in Thongkam Market, known for northern khanom jeen rice vermicelli with curries, especially tangy pork nam ngiao. The stall also serves other curries over noodles or rice and northern dishes; its market seating and self-service style make this a simple local meal stop.
whyGo: Try khanom jeen nam ngiao, a northern-style tomato and pork curry broth served over fermented rice vermicelli.
Choose among several curries, including coconut curry, green curry chicken and the mixed nam lo; rice can replace noodles.
The MICHELIN Guide recognizes the stall and lists it in its lowest price tier; market-side vegetables are described as unlimited.
Expect an informal market meal: order and pay at the counter, find a seat, and return dishes after eating.
bestFor: Travelers curious about northern Thai noodle curries and informal market dining
A low-cost lunch or dinner around San Pa Khoi and the east bank of the Ping River
Groups who want a choice of curries, including some that are less spicy than nam ngiao
skipIf: You require confirmed vegetarian, vegan, halal or allergy-safe food; meat stock, fish sauce and shared utensils may be used.
You need confirmed step-free access, accessible seating or an accessible toilet.
You prefer table service, a quiet dining room or a fully documented English menu.
duration: Allow 30–60 minutes for the meal and any queue; this is a planning estimate.
cost: Budget roughly ฿30–100 per person for a bowl or plate and a simple extra; drinks and add-ons cost more. Recent customer reports cite dishes from about ฿30 and under ฿100, but this is not a venue-published December 2026 menu.
hours: The MICHELIN Guide currently lists Monday–Saturday 11:00–23:00 and Sunday closed. Recheck close to travel, especially during the year-end holidays.
bestTime: Go mid-afternoon or outside the main lunch and dinner rush for a better chance of a seat. Arrive well before closing in case a curry sells out.
gettingThere: The stall is inside Thongkam Market, 11 Soi Thasatoi, Chang Moi, on the east side of the Ping River. From the Old City, take a red songthaew, tuk-tuk or ride-hail to the market and walk to the stall; allow around 10–20 minutes by car depending on traffic (estimate, not a published transit time). Save the map pin or Thai name ขนมจีนสันป่าข่อย to show the driver.
booking: No advance booking is indicated for this casual market stall. The MICHELIN Guide lists it as cash only; bring small baht notes. It lists +66 61 301 8000 for enquiries.
accessibility: No reliable accessibility statement was found. Market aisles and seating are informal, and step-free access, aisle width and toilet facilities are unverified. Contact the venue if access needs are important.
practicalTips: Start with khanom jeen nam ngiao for the northern tomato-based curry; other curry toppings, chicken khao soi and rice options are also reported.
The signature nam ngiao is pork-based. Ask staff directly about ingredients and shared utensils; no vegetarian, halal or allergen-safe preparation is confirmed.
The usual format is counter ordering and payment, followed by self-service seating; return dishes after eating.
Carry cash and allow flexibility for a queue, seating and which curries remain available.
decemberNotes: This is an everyday food stall, not a seasonal event. No December 2026 holiday schedule is published; verify opening around Christmas and New Year before making a special trip.
uncertainties: Current regular hours are listed by MICHELIN, but temporary closures and December 2026 holiday hours are unknown.
Prices are drawn from recent customer reports and may change; the restaurant has no dated official menu available in the sources checked.
Transit times are planning estimates and depend on traffic; no dedicated public-transit route information was confirmed.
